source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the priority nursing assessment after an EGD with sedation?
questions.rationale: Withhold food and fluids until the gag reflex returns; monitor LOC, vitals, and SpO2.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EGD (PDF p. 340)
questions.quote: After the patient's gag reflex has returned

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which position is used during EGD?
questions.rationale: Left lateral position facilitates clearance of secretions and smooth scope entry.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EGD (PDF p. 340)
questions.quote: The patient is positioned in the left lateral position

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After EGD, which finding suggests perforation?
questions.rationale: Report pain, bleeding, unusual difficulty swallowing, and rapidly rising temperature.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EGD (PDF p. 340)
questions.quote: Rapidly elevated temperature

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: GERD is primarily caused by:
questions.rationale: Backflow of gastric contents occurs through an incompetent LES.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GERD (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: due to incompetent lower esophageal sphincter

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which instruction helps a client with GERD?
questions.rationale: Elevate the bed, avoid eating 2 hours before bed, avoid tight clothing and lying after meals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GERD Nursing Management (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: Elevate head of bed on 6 to 8 inches.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug class is more potent than H2 blockers for reducing gastric acid?
questions.rationale: PPIs (omeprazole) inhibit the parietal cell ATPase pump and are more potent.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GERD Pharmacology (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: More potent than H2 receptor antagonists

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Nissen fundoplication treats GERD by:
questions.rationale: A portion of the fundus is wrapped around the sphincter area.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GERD Surgery (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: Wrapping of a portion of the gastric fundus around the sphincter area of the esophagus.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Barrett's esophagus is significant because it is a precursor to:
questions.rationale: Chronic reflux changes squamous lining (metaplasia), a precursor to esophageal cancer.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Barrett's Esophagus (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: Precursor to esophageal cancer

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with hiatal hernia should be taught to:
options: Not recline for 1 hour after eating
questions.rationale: Small frequent feedings; do not recline 1 hour after eating; elevate head of bed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hiatal Hernia (PDF p. 342)
questions.quote: Patient is advised not to recline for 1 hour after eating

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Epigastric pain 2–3 hours after meals relieved by eating suggests:
questions.rationale: Duodenal ulcer pain occurs 2–3 hours after meals and is relieved by food.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Duodenal vs Gastric Ulcer (PDF p. 342)
questions.quote: Pain occurs 2-3 hrs after meal

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is more typical of gastric ulcer than duodenal ulcer?
questions.rationale: Gastric ulcer: pain after eating, vomiting, hematemesis, weight loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Duodenal vs Gastric Ulcer (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: Hematemesis more common than melena

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which organism is a major cause of peptic ulcer and gastritis?
questions.rationale: H. pylori is treated with antibiotics (amoxicillin, clarithromycin) plus a PPI.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Peptic Ulcer Disease (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: Gram-negative bacteria (H. Pylori)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with gastritis develops hematemesis, tachycardia, and hypotension. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: These indicate hemorrhagic gastritis; notify the physician.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gastritis Nursing Management (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: Notify the physician if signs of hemorrhagic gastritis are present.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Severe peptic ulcers with extreme hyperacidity from a gastrin-secreting tumor is:
questions.rationale: Zollinger-Ellison: gastrinoma causing hyperacidity and severe ulcers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: Consists of severe peptic ulcers, extreme gastric hyperacidity

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sucralfate protects an ulcer by:
questions.rationale: Cytoprotectants form a viscous barrier that binds to the ulcer surface.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cytoprotectants (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: forms a protective barrier, binds to the surface of the ulcer

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Billroth II surgery involves:
questions.rationale: Billroth II is gastrojejunostomy; Billroth I is gastroduodenostomy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PUD Surgery (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Billroth II (Gastrojejunostomy)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Thirty minutes after eating, a post-gastrectomy client has palpitations, sweating, and diarrhea. This is:
questions.rationale: Rapid gastric emptying causes dumping syndrome symptoms about 30 minutes after meals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dumping Syndrome (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Symptoms occurring 30 minutes after eating

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching helps prevent dumping syndrome?
questions.rationale: Take fluids 1 hour before or after meals, eat dry low-carbohydrate meals, and lie down after.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dumping Syndrome (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Fluid intake with meals is discouraged

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Diverticula most commonly occur in the:
questions.rationale: Diverticula occur most commonly in the sigmoid colon.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diverticular Disease (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Most commonly occur in the sigmoid colon.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for diverticulosis without inflammation?
questions.rationale: High fiber for diverticulosis; low fiber may be needed during acute diverticulitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diverticular Disease (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: soft, high fiber foods are indicated for diverticulosis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the diagnostic test of choice for diverticulitis?
questions.rationale: CT is the test of choice in diverticulitis and reveals abscesses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diverticular Disease (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: CT Scan (test of choice for diverticulitis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Transmural inflammation with a cobblestone appearance, mostly in the ileum, describes:
questions.rationale: Crohn's affects all layers, skip areas, fistulas, cobblestone mucosa.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Crohn's Disease (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: (Classic cobblestone appearance)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ten to 20 bloody liquid stools daily with LLQ cramping suggests:
questions.rationale: Ulcerative colitis involves mucosa of colon and rectum with bloody diarrhea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ulcerative Colitis (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: Diarrhea (10 to 20 liquid stools per day)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for inflammatory bowel disease?
questions.rationale: Low residue, high protein, high calorie, with vitamins and iron.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IBD Nursing Interventions (PDF p. 346)
questions.quote: Low residue

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which surgery for ulcerative colitis creates a continent internal ileal reservoir?
questions.rationale: Kock pouch is a continent ileal reservoir with a stoma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IBD Surgery (PDF p. 346)
questions.quote: Continent Ileostomy (Kock ileostomy)
